title: Throughput Playground — interactive dev sandbox for inference tradeoffs
content:
Context / problem: Engineers and product folks keep guessing how batching, quantization, routing, and KV/prefix caching interact for their real workload. Benchmarks (norm seq lengths, puppet queries) are useful but don’t map to app mixes. Need a lightweight interactive tool in Console to simulate realistic request mixes and show clear tradeoffs: tokens/sec, 95th pctl latency, per-token cost, and error modes when falling back to cheaper models or regions.

Goal: a dev-facing playground where you can: upload a small workload (JSON of requests or example prompts), choose model variants (fp16 / int8 / q4), turn on/off KV caching, set batching policy (max batch size, wait ms), pick routing policy (latency-first, cost-first, region preference), and then run a fast simulation that returns latency/cost histograms and suggested knob changes.

Key UX pieces (sketch):
- Left column: workload input (paste requests, load sample workloads, preset templates: chat, search-embedding, rerank) + sliders for distribution (short/medium/long).
- Middle: live config controls: model selector, quantization toggle, batch size slider, max-wait ms, cache hit rate slider, dedicated vs hosted toggle, autoscale headroom slider.
- Right: results pane: summary KPIs (mean latency, 95p, throughput, unit cost), cost breakdown by tokens / model / batch inefficiency, latency distribution chart, a small table of problematic requests (largest latencies) and suggested remediations.
- Bottom: compare view to snapshot previous run — diff graphs and a compact scorecard.

User stories (rough):
- As an ML infra engineer, I want to see how increasing batch size affects 95p latency for our conversational traffic so I can pick a safe batching policy.
- As a product owner, I want a quick estimate of monthly cost delta if we quantize to q4 and accept 3% quality drop.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to show a customer the effect of moving some traffic to Dedicated GPUs vs Hosted burst capacity.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Upload workload or pick a preset; run simulation within ~10s for small workloads (<=100 requests).
- Show throughput, mean/95p latencies, and a cost estimate with itemized line items.
- Allow toggling model variant + batch + cache and rerun quickly; keep history of last 5 runs.

Open questions / risks:
- Fidelity: simulation must be lightweight (approximate) but useful; how to calibrate to real-traffic hardware profiles? (Need mapping from model profile to latency/throughput numbers maintained by serving-runtime team.)
- QoS and fallback modeling: how do we simulate model fallback behavior (e.g., fallback to smaller model under overload)? Represent as a probability or deterministic threshold?
- Security: uploaded workloads may contain PII — ensure workspace marked ephemeral and optionally scrubbed.

Telemetry / metrics to capture: workload type, average seq length, cache hit assumptions, model variant, knob deltas, report downloaded, export snapshot. Tag with customer (for SGEs) only when user opts in.

Implementation notes / quick plan:
- Phase 0: prototype as a client-side simulator using server-hosted latency profiles (JSON) + simple batching model. No heavy backend. UI in Console: simple React panel.
- Phase 1: integrate real runtime profiles from eng-serving-runtime, allow sampling of dedicated vs hosted latency curves, add compare snapshots, and enable export to support bundle.
- Nice-to-have: tie suggestions into Optimize (recommended quantization/batching for this workload) and create a quick 'apply to route' flow to push a canary config.

Next steps (for me):
- build a toy workload (50 mixed seqs) from live anonymized traces — ask SRE for sanitized sample.
- mock first UI in Figma (quick 3 panels).
- sync with Sam (runtime batch model) and Rhea (console infra) next Wed.

Notes to self: keep language simple in UI (avoid deep infra jargon), show concrete tradeoffs ("saves ~$X / month but 95p latency +Y ms"), and allow saving presets (customer playbooks).

TODOs:
- [ ] Draft Figma screens
- [ ] Request sanitized trace sample from SRE
- [ ] Wireframe API shape for latency profiles
- [ ] Prototype client-side sim + demo data

Rough priorities: MVP sim + UI (2 sprints), runtime profile hookup (1 sprint), Optimize integration (stretch).

End of jot.
